'''Hend the Striker''' is a Hero of the Horn.

==Appearance and Personality==
He is a large, dark-skinned man. He carries a hammer in one hand and a spike in the other. He rides a big bay horse and laughs a lot, even in battle.{{ref/book|14|39}}

==Activities==
He is one of the Heroes of the Horn who are called back to fight in the [[Last Battle]].{{ref/book|14|39}} He is also the one to explain to [[Mat Cauthon]] that he is not a Hero of the Horn.{{ref/book|14|43}}

==Parallels==
[[File:76a772b7-6aa6-42c6-af4a-fc13e7a7d5fdHiResProxy.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A statue of John Henry at the Great Bend Tunnel at the John Henry Park in Talcott, West Virginia, U.S.A.]]Hend is based on the popular American folk hero of African descent [[Wikipedia:John Henry (folklore)|John Henry]] who drove railroad spikes with a hammer.{{ref/book|origins|Hend the Striker}} According to legend, John Henry's prowess as a steel driver was measured in a race against a steam-powered rock drill, a race that he won only to die in victory with a hammer in hand as his heart gave out from stress. Inkeeping with Jordan's theme of events turning to legend, the true facts of John Henry's life are disputed.
